edge_explainer: TAPE: the house premise was built on when-issued prints. FedEx's 05-13 press release states the when-issued window ran 05-27 to the close of 05-29 under 'FDXF WI'; the completion 8-K (acc. 0001104659-26-068521) puts the Effective Time at 12:01am CT on 2026-06-01. The 05-28 bar that produced the $185 'early high' traded 3,268 SHARES. Real regular-way series starts 06-01 at $149.53 (3.62M shares), peaked at $188.46 on 06-09, low close $137.55 on 07-30, now $139.02 — a true -26.2% drawdown, 63 days out, and the low is TWO SESSIONS OLD. This is not a base. FLOW: 'FORCED_BUY_INVERTED' names the wrong mechanism — FDX was already in the S&P 500 and FDXF joined it, so index funds received the shares in kind at index weight and bought nothing; mechanical index flow is NULL. (FDXF did replace American Airlines in the Dow Jones Transportation Average, a rounding error against a $20.8B cap.) THE FLOW FACT THE GENERATOR MISSED: FedEx distributed only 80.1% and RETAINED UP TO 19.9%, ~30M shares = ~$4.17B = roughly 59 TRADING DAYS OF ADV, which it 'must generally dispose of within 24 months' via debt-for-equity exchanges with FedEx creditors or a split-off exchange offer — the latter priced at a discount by construction. The guided 149.5M share count explicitly includes those 30M shares. CAP STRUCTURE: $4.264B total debt ($3.70B senior unsecured notes at 4.30/4.65/4.95/5.25% plus a $600M term loan fully drawn 05-27), weighted average 4.79%, $1.2B revolver undrawn, $250M cash, operating leases ~$1.47B, DTL $318M, TOTAL EQUITY NEGATIVE at -$562M — because ~$4.1B of cash was dividended to FedEx before the Effective Time. HONESTY FINDING (takeaway vs the issuer's own data, twice in one release): (1) 'Revenue was $2.4 billion, a 4.8% increase' while average daily shipments fell 5.9% — the release itself attributes the gain to fuel surcharges and weight per shipment; volumes have now fallen four straight years, 99.7k/day FY23 to 86.1k FY26, -13.6%. (2) 'Operating margin of 9.0% to 9.5% compared to 7.8%' is guided alongside 'adjusted operating margin of 11.5% to 12.0% compared to 11.8%' — on the COMPARABLE measure the company guides FLAT TO 30BPS DOWN, and the GAAP 'expansion' is entirely the non-recurrence of $130M of spin costs. Management's own bridge (deck slide 8) confirms it: 11.8% -> ~11.8%, from Net Yield +200bps, Efficiency +80bps, Variable Comp -130bps, TSA -120bps, Net Volume -30bps. Year one of the standalone plan delivers ZERO adjusted margin improvement. THE FRAGILE PLANK: +200bps of net yield is over half the positive bridge, and the peer tape just repriced exactly that — SAIA's Q2 CY26 8-K printed revenue/cwt EX-FUEL at -2.2% while buying +8.4% tonnage, ODFL held price and gave up 5.7% of shipments, ArcBest announced a 07-16 restructuring, and Amazon expanded nationwide LTL on 06-10. SELF-CORRECTION: my first read attributed the July slide to an LTL demand break; the primary Q2 prints REFUTE that — ODFL (OR 70.1% vs 74.6%), SAIA (86.9% vs 87.8%) and XPO (NA LTL OI +43.2%) all EXPANDED margins. The group de-rated on PRICE, not demand, and FDXF is the only one whose margin collapsed. VALUATION: 149.5M shares x $139.02 = $20.78B cap, net debt $4.014B, EV $24.80B; FY26 adjusted operating income $1,108M -> 22.4x EV/adj-EBIT, in line with SAIA at ~21x on a comparable 87.4 adjusted operating ratio — fair-to-full, not cheap. Annualised TY26 EPS ex-spin-cost $4.11-4.46 -> 31-34x, against a Form 10 pro forma FY25 EPS of $6.06, i.e. run-rate earnings are ~28% BELOW the pro forma base. DISCLOSURE GAP: there is NO dollar estimate of standalone public-company costs anywhere in the Form 10 — the pro formas carry a $0 autonomous-entity adjustment on an $8.8B carve-out, which is an assumption, not a measurement.
